newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Germany faces claims for millions from tourists.
newsitem.headline: Germany faces claims for millions from tourists.

text.p: The German government faces claims for more than 10 million marks ($6.56 million) from thousands of tourists who lost out when travel companies with whom they had booked holidays went bankrupt.
The European Court of Justice said on Tuesday that Germany's failure to introduce in time European Union law to protect tourists from such bankruptcies made it liable for the stranded travellers.
A spokeswoman for the Justice Ministry in Bonn confirmed there were around 6,000 claims lodged for about 10 million marks following the collapses of a series of tour operators in 1993 and 1994.
The German government would try to settle the claims out of court and as quickly as possible, she added.
The European court said an EU state's failure to transpose a directive within the time required was a serious breach of Community law which gave rise to liability.
The directive required Germany to enact the EU rules no later than December 1992, but it only did so in June 1994 following the collapse MP Travel Line International and other tour operators.

The German court must now decide the issue of damages but the European court has rejected the German government's argument that airline tickets or hotel vouchers provide sufficient security against a bankrupt travel agency. ($1=1.5252 Mark)
